method: Bunching ratio = awards in the four 2%-of-the-line bins just under a line / a cubic Poisson curve fitted outside the bins near any threshold value in force that year or the year before and outside bins holding a multiple of the line's leading power of ten. Window 0.6 to 1.4 times the line. Poisson bootstrap, 200 replicates. Changes: two years before vs two years after (each agency's own date for the 2018 civilian change); DiD = change at the new line minus change at the old line.

universes.micro_purchase: all purchase orders and definitive contracts. The FPDS reporting floor moves with this line, so counts just under it are thinned by non-reporting: read changes with care
universes.simplified_acquisition: all purchase orders and definitive contracts
universes.synopsis: all purchase orders and definitive contracts (posting applies to sole-source actions too)
universes.cost_or_pricing_data: not competed (extent competed B, C, E, G) and not commercial (commercial procedures code D): where certified data could apply. The 2026 move to $10M is Defense (and Coast Guard) only
universes.commercial_simplified: commercial items (commercial procedures code A, B or C)
universes.subcontracting_plan: not set aside for small business (no set-aside code), not construction (product or service code not Y or Z)
universes.subcontracting_plan_construction: not set aside, construction or real-property repair (product or service code Y or Z)
universes.justification_level1: other than full and open competition (extent competed B, C, E), excluding 8(a) awards (statutory exception)
universes.8a_competitive_threshold_nonmfg: 8(a) sole-source awards (set-aside code 8AN) outside manufacturing (NAICS not 31-33)

not_scanned.micro_purchase_construction / micro_purc: never changed in the period, and the data cannot tell which purchases fall under Davis-Bacon or the Service Contract Act
not_scanned.micro_purchase_contingency_us / _abroad: apply only to contingency, emergency or university purchases, which the data does not identify
not_scanned.synopsis_display_floor: a notice-display rule with little reason to shape award values; moves on the same days as the micro-purchase line (left in as an excluded value in every fit)
not_scanned.commercial_simplified_13_500c: applies only to special purchases (contingency, defense against attack) the data does not identify
not_scanned.cost_or_pricing_data_pre2018_contracts: applies to modifications of contracts entered into before July 2018, not to new awards
not_scanned.justification_dod_statute_*: statute-only change of 2025-12-18 that FAR 6.304 has not implemented; at most part of one Defense year after it, with Defense data published 90 days late

caveats: A pile-up is a pattern, not proof of why it happens: budgets written to fit the rules, set-aside rules tied to a line, and contract splitting all produce it.

Many lines move on the same day (1 October of 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2025): see same_day_changes. A change test on one line is confounded by the others that moved with it, and the first day of a fiscal year has its own pattern.
Justification level 1 and the subcontracting plan have had the same value since 2010 and change on the same days; their universes overlap, so their results are not independent.
The FPDS reporting floor moves with the micro-purchase line, so counts just under it change for reporting reasons too.
Samples near the larger lines (above about $10 million) are small; level 3 justifications and the 8(a) justification line are mostly too thin to test.
Delivery orders and BPA calls are not in the data; contract vehicles are left out. Values are base and all options at award, which is close to but not the same as each rule's measure.
Defense data are published 90 days late, so the latest Defense fiscal year is incomplete.

Placebo values are round numbers that were never thresholds; near $3 million to $15 million thresholds are so dense that no free value exists, and those lines rely on the active-versus-inactive comparison only.
